title: Open Bandit Sample, BTS Value from Random Logs
subtitle: ZOZOTOWN all-campaign sample shipped with obp, 10,000 rounds per policy, 2,000 bootstrap replicates

rows.label: IPS
rows.detail: Bootstrap 95 percent CI 1.49 to 9.50 per 1,000. Relative error against the on-policy rate 8.4 percent

rows.label: SNIPS
rows.detail: Bootstrap 95 percent CI 1.57 to 9.87 per 1,000. Relative error against the on-policy rate 13.7 percent

rows.label: DM, LightGBM
rows.detail: Bootstrap 95 percent CI 4.70 to 4.79 per 1,000. Relative error against the on-policy rate 13.0 percent

rows.label: DR, LightGBM
rows.detail: Bootstrap 95 percent CI 1.68 to 9.84 per 1,000. Relative error against the on-policy rate 15.7 percent

rows.label: Switch-DR, tau 10
rows.detail: Bootstrap 95 percent CI 3.30 to 6.21 per 1,000. Relative error against the on-policy rate 9.8 percent

rows.label: Random policy, own rate
rows.detail: 38 clicks in 10,000 random-policy impressions, the data every estimate above is built from

caption: All five estimates land inside the on-policy BTS interval of 3.0 to 5.5 clicks per 1,000. That is a sanity check, not a ranking. The random log holds 38 clicks, so IPS, SNIPS and DR have intervals roughly 1.5 to 9.9 per 1,000 wide. DM's narrow interval reflects only resampling of rounds, not reward-model error. Hover a bar for its interval.
source: the project's off-policy evaluation on the Open Bandit Dataset
